for order in orders {
    let lines = db.lines_of_order(order.id)?;
findings.recommendation: Fetch the lines of every order in one query with the existing batch method `db.lines_of_orders(&ids)` (api/src/db.rs:31, `WHERE order_id = ANY($1)`), collecting the ids from `orders` first, then group the lines by `order_id` (e.g. a HashMap<i64, i64> of totals) and build the summaries in the order of `orders`, so ordering and results stay unchanged. Cost today: 1 + N queries per request, N up to 100 orders, on a user-facing path that runs on every customer page view (proposal `## Domains`); with the batch call it is 2 queries whatever N. Alternatively, compute the totals in SQL with `SUM(quantity * unit_price_cents) ... GROUP BY order_id`.
